p: Leeds has some brilliant extras to pair with a round of jungle golf. Kirkstall Abbey, a short trip from the centre, is a remarkably well-preserved medieval Cistercian abbey and a lovely place to explore, with riverside grounds for a picnic. Tropical World at Roundhay keeps the jungle theme going, with butterflies, meerkats and warm glasshouses full of exotic plants. Kids love it, and it's perfect if the weather turns.

The Thackray Museum of Medicine is another fascinating stop, with interactive galleries that bring the history of health and medicine to life. It's a bit gory in places, which, let's be honest, older kids will think is the best bit. Allow a couple of hours to do it justice.

For the golf, here's how to get ahead. Take a moment to read each hole, looking for slopes and angles. Use the walls for clever rebounds, and keep your putts smooth and gentle. A big whack might look impressive, but it rarely ends well. With younger players, agree a shot limit per hole before you start so the game flows nicely and nobody gets stuck.

Add a meal out in the city afterwards and you've got a varied day that covers everything from history to hole-in-ones. Not bad for a day in Yorkshire, whatever the weather decides to do. And if anyone grumbles about losing, remind them there's always a rematch next time you're in town.
